newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah eyes liquidity, BI governor.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah eyes liquidity, BI governor.

text.p: * Indonesian rupiah steady, swaps rise amid tight liquidity as market awaits speech by central bank governor.
* Malaysian ringgit and Thai baht slip as dollar surges above 1.56 marks in morning trade.
* Singapore dollar unaffected by U.S. dollar gains on dearth of trading interest.
The Indonesian rupiah remained relatively stable in slow Tuesday trade as operators kept an eye on liquidity conditions and the possibility of a higher central bank fixing.
Dealers in Jakarta said a relatively tight market seemed to have driven up short-dated swaps, prompting longer-term rates to follow suit.
One local bank dealer said trading in the spot market was slow, with some state banks seen unloading dollars on customer orders and not for trading purposes.
"It's a thin market. There was some selling interest from some state banks at the 2,345.75 level," the dealer said.
He said the central bank might raise its fixing again in the afternoon because the dollar was surging against the yen.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,345/2,537 and the conversion rate to 2,345/2,393 on Monday.
Some dealers seemed to link the scheduled appearance of the central bank governor at a seminar in the afternoon to a possible announcement of a band widening.
But central bank sources said there was no such plan. They said the governor was scheduled to speak on economic prospects for next year along with other economists.
"Dollar/rupiah is a non-event because we're hugging the lower side of the intervention band. The market is afraid of a band widening," said a Japanese bank dealer in Singapore.
Some rumours also had the governor calling for a press conference, but central bank officials denied this as well.
Dealers said the market was swirling with rumours but, surprisingly, this was not reflected much in spot rates.
"The market is rather quiet and thin in volume," one said.
In Malaysia, the ringgit slid to a low of 2.5300 against the dollar as the U.S. unit shot above 1.5600 marks on stop-loss buying after overnight gains.
A Singapore dealer said dollar/ringgit would be supported at 2.5280 with strong resistance expected at 2.5320/30.
The market largely ignored forecasts of lower current account deficits and a stronger ringgit in 1997 by a Malaysian government-backed think tank, dealers said.

"People are bullish on the ringgit but because of year-end factors, there's a lot of dollar demand. So they're waiting for that to finish before getting into the ringgit again," said the Singapore dealer.
The Singapore dollar remained stubbornly resilient to the U.S. dollar's gains in the face of commercial U.S. dollar selling interest around S$1.4025/30.
"A lot of people are frustrated with being long dollar/Sing because when the dollar/majors came up 100 points, dollar/Sing hardly moved," said the dealer.
He said players would opt to go long the U.S. dollar against the majors rather than against the Sing dollar, where prospects for gains were so limited.
The Thai baht fell to 25.572-25.575 at 0425 GMT against 25.535-540 late on Monday on continued demand for the dollar.
The Bank of Thailand (BOT) fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.56, the lowest fixing since January 6, 1993 when the mid-rate was at 25.57. The mid-rate was set at 25.51 on Monday.
Thai money market liquidity tightened on the back of recent bank buying of the rising dollar, dealers said.
The BOT governor's statement on Monday that the central bank would try to stabilise short-term interest rates to ensure that long-term rates continued to drop did not affect sentiment.

"The BOT, the new government lineup have all been saying they want lower rates to stabilise the economy. Dollar/baht swaps have already been reflective of this for the past few days," said a Singapore-based dealer.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
